evals.name: bare-invocation-is-read-only-inventory
evals.expected_output: Routes to check (the default action) and reports two things without writing anything: the override inventory — bundled defaults available to override, which ones the consuming repo already overrides, and for each existing override whether it is byte-identical to the current bundled default — and the effective artifact layout read from the consuming project's CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules, falling back to the default songwriting/ layout.
expectations: Defaults to check when no action argument is given, rather than prompting for an action or scaffolding anything
Lists the bundled defaults under ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/context/pat-pattison/templates/ and the overrides present under ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/songwriting/templates/pat-pattison/
Applies the convention-resolution ladder: an override present wins; with no override the bundled default stays in force as the safe default
Flags each byte-identical override as INFO — it customizes nothing and only opts the repo out of future improvements — and names `apply remove <name>` as the way to clear it
Reads the consuming project's CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules for a declared songwriting layout and reports the effective layout, defaulting to songwriting/ when none is declared
Creates, copies, and deletes nothing — check is read-only

evals.name: diverged-override-collision-confirms-before-clobbering
evals.prompt: /songwriting:setup apply scaffold co-write-session-opener metaphor-recipe-prompt — I already edited songwriting/templates/pat-pattison/co-write-session-opener.md heavily. Just overwrite both from the bundled defaults.
evals.expected_output: Runs check first, then splits the two names by collision state: metaphor-recipe-prompt is not yet overridden so it is scaffolded non-interactively, while the already-diverged co-write-session-opener triggers the destructive-collision guard — it shows the difference and refuses to overwrite without explicit confirmation in this conversation, despite the standing 'just overwrite' instruction.
expectations: Runs the check inventory before acting on either name
Scaffolds the not-yet-overridden metaphor-recipe-prompt non-interactively — that is a safe path, not a collision
Does NOT overwrite the existing diverged co-write-session-opener override: it shows the difference and asks for explicit confirmation in this conversation first
Names the reason for the carve-out: overwriting a diverged override would lose the consumer's own edits

Copies each scaffolded bundled default verbatim as the starting point for the consumer to edit, creating songwriting/templates/pat-pattison/ if absent, and confirms the scaffolded files are tracked and not gitignored
Re-runs the check inventory afterward and reports the resulting override set

evals.name: refuses-bulk-scaffold-of-every-bundled-default
evals.prompt: /songwriting:setup apply — scaffold all sixteen bundled templates so I have the full set locally, then delete songwriting/templates/pat-pattison/worksheet-prompt.md which I rewrote last week.
evals.expected_output: Declines the blanket scaffold as the documented anti-pattern — an override freezes that template, so sixteen verbatim copies opt the repo out of future plugin improvements while customizing nothing — and asks which templates the consumer actually intends to change; the named removal of a customized override hits the same destructive-collision guard, so it shows what would be lost and confirms first rather than deleting.
expectations: Declines to scaffold all sixteen bundled defaults and names it as an anti-pattern: sixteen files that opt out of updates while customizing nothing
Gives the mechanism — an override freezes that template, so the craft skills load it instead of the bundled default forever and later plugin improvements stop reaching this repo
Asks which specific templates the consumer intends to customize instead of scaffolding a set the consumer did not name
Does not delete the customized worksheet-prompt override outright: shows what would be lost and confirms first, because it is diverged rather than byte-identical
States that removing a byte-identical override is the safe, non-interactive path, in contrast to this one

evals.name: apply-with-no-target-changes-nothing
evals.expected_output: Reports the current inventory and changes nothing: apply acts only on the names given in scaffold/remove arguments, so an apply with no target is an inventory report, and re-running it is idempotent.
expectations: Writes and deletes nothing — no template is scaffolded and none is removed
Reports the current override inventory, the same content check would report
States that apply acts only on named scaffold/remove arguments and never scaffolds or removes a template the consumer did not name
Does not invent a default set of templates to scaffold in the absence of arguments
Re-running the command yields the same report rather than accumulating changes

evals.name: custom-layout-is-guidance-not-an-edit
evals.prompt: /songwriting:setup apply — we keep craft artifacts in docs/lyrics/ instead. Put that convention wherever the plugin needs it so the craft skills pick it up.
evals.expected_output: Shows the one-line convention for the consumer to add to their OWN CLAUDE.md or rules and stops there: the artifact layout is a read/confirm-only surface for this skill, and the plugin carries no userConfig, so there is nowhere else for the value to go — it edits neither the consumer's instruction surface nor any machine-local or plugin-side state.
expectations: Does not edit the consumer's CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules — that surface is consumer-owned; setup reads and reports it, it does not author it
Shows the one-line convention text for the consumer to add themselves
States that the plugin carries no userConfig, so the layout is not a plugin option to be set
Writes no machine-local state — nothing in the plugin directory or the plugin data directory
Confirms that template overrides are the only thing this skill writes, and that they are tracked team-shared config in the consumer's repo
Reports the effective layout that is in force now, rather than claiming the new layout is already active
